planting.note: Plant divisions or rooted cuttings after the last frost in moist, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Kentucky Colonel is a large-leaved spearmint selection traditionally used for mint juleps and grows best confined to a container or bed with a root barrier, since mint spreads aggressively.

directions: Plant divisions in moist, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, ideally in a container or a bed edged with a root barrier, since mint spreads aggressively by rhizome and can quickly overrun a garden bed. Kentucky Colonel is a spearmint selection with unusually large, crinkled, dark green leaves and a smooth, sweet, mild mint flavor without the sharper bite of peppermint, making it the traditional choice among Southern bartenders and home mixologists for mint juleps and other cocktails where a clean, refined mint character matters. It is also excellent for iced tea, fresh garnishes, and simple syrups. Keep soil consistently moist, since mint wilts quickly in dry conditions, and cut back hard in mid-summer if growth becomes leggy to encourage a fresh flush of tender new leaves. In light shade the leaves stay more tender and less prone to leaf spot than in full, hot Gulf South sun.
sources: Southern Living — Kentucky Colonel Mint for Mint Juleps
